- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high, then apply mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish within 3–5 days, model often lags; forecast should adjust upward by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 7-day average is below 30-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days if trend persists.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly diverging (e.g., >0.8 then drops to <0.2); if sentiment shifts, adjust forecast by 2–4% in opposite direction of sentiment change.
